records.subject: Hydrogel e-skin
records.quote: Herein, we proposed a hydrogel e-skin that realizes high-resolution spatial mapping of temperature and pressure by constructing an electrode array-thermogalvanic hydrogel (TG hydrogel)-electrode array sandwich structure.

records.subject: Electrode array–thermogalvanic hydrogel–electrode array sandwich
records.object: High-resolution spatial mapping of temperature and pressure
records.quote: Herein, we proposed a hydrogel e-skin that realizes high-resolution spatial mapping of temperature and pressure by constructing an electrode array-thermogalvanic hydrogel (TG hydrogel)-electrode array sandwich structure.

records.subject: Horizontal thermogalvanic effect of the redox couple
records.quote: This hydrogel e-skin achieves temperature and pressure dual sensing through the thermogalvanic and piezoresistive effect of the redox couple in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively.
records.conditions: In the hydrogel e-skin; horizontal direction.

records.subject: Vertical piezoresistive effect of the redox couple
records.quote: This hydrogel e-skin achieves temperature and pressure dual sensing through the thermogalvanic and piezoresistive effect of the redox couple in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively.
records.conditions: In the hydrogel e-skin; vertical direction.

records.subject: Horizontal reference electrode for temperature sensing
records.quote: A reference electrode for temperature sensing is introduced in the horizontal direction, so that the temperature shift of the bottom electrode under external thermal stimulus will no longer affect the accuracy of thermal perception.
records.conditions: Under external thermal stimulus.

records.subject: Bottom-electrode temperature shift under external thermal stimulus

records.subject: Reduced hydrogel thickness

records.subject: Dexterous robot hand covered with hydrogel e-skin

records.subject: 1-Allyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ionic liquid
records.object: Solid-to-liquid phase transition across cold and hot regions
records.quote: Here, we present an ionic thermogalvanic cell using an ionic liquid, 1-allyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride.
context_quotes: The ionic liquid undergoes a phase transition from solid to liquid in cold and hot regions, significantly improving performance without requiring additional components or complex processing.
records.conditions: In the ionic thermogalvanic cell.

records.subject: Solid-to-liquid phase transition across cold and hot regions

records.subject: Phase-transitional ionic thermogalvanic cell
records.quote: Compared to a homogeneous liquid-state cell, the phase-transitional system exhibits a 2.2-fold increase in the Seebeck coefficient (from 1.79 to 3.89 mV/K), a 3.66-fold enhancement in the power output (from 4.3 to 15.9 nW), and 3.47-fold improvement in the figure of merit (from 0.15 to 0.52) under the same temperature difference of 20 degrees C.
records.conditions: Compared with a homogeneous liquid-state cell at the same temperature difference of 20 °C.

records.subject: Ion aggregation near the two electrodes
records.quote: To address this knowledge gap, we prepared typical hydrogel thermocells consisting of graphite electrodes and polyacrylamide (PAAm) hydrogel with K-3[Fe(CN)(6)]/K-4[Fe(CN)(6)] redox pair electrolytes.
context_quotes: The above experiments indicate that the energy storage characteristic of hydrogel thermocells originate from the aggregation of ions near the two electrodes during thermoelectric conversion process, but charge storage is achieved by the gel structure to hinder the ion transport and concentration equilibrium after the removing of the temperature difference.

records.quote: We then built a test bench to investigate the energy storage characteristics of hydrogel thermocells under various parametric conditions, including the effects of electrode temperature difference, electrode average temperature, shelving duration, redox pair ion concentration and hydrogel thickness.
context_quotes: The thermally induced energy storage performance is greatly affected by above parameters, for example, the areal capacitance and the energy storage coefficient both decreased by about 57.5 % when the temperature difference of the electrode increases from 10 degrees C similar to to 30 degrees C.
modality_evidence: We then built a test bench to investigate the energy storage characteristics of hydrogel thermocells under various parametric conditions, including the effects of electrode temperature difference, electrode average temperature, shelving duration, redox pair ion concentration and hydrogel thickness.
